May 8, 2010
Sandra Flores
Chief Operating Officer
Poole, Mcknight and Rush
Dear Ms. Flores:
This letter sets down the terms on which our firm will carry out a review of the
supply chain that Poole, Mcknight and Rush depends on, and it becomes our
agreement at the moment you countersign the enclosed copy and return it to me. I
have written the terms out in full and in ordinary language, in the conviction that an
assignment of this kind runs more surely when both sides have read the same
account of it before any work begins, and that the few hours spent reconciling
expectations at the outset are repaid many times over in the months that follow. I
would ask you to weigh what follows against your own understanding of the
assignment, and to tell me, before you sign, of anything on which the two do not
agree.
Scope of the Work and Our Approach
The assignment is a review of how Poole, Mcknight and Rush sources, moves, and
holds the goods on which its operations rest, and its object is a clear and defensible
account of where the present arrangement serves the business well and where it
quietly costs more than it returns. We will begin by establishing a faithful picture of
the supply chain as it actually runs today, following the flow from supplier through
to the point of use, and setting the cost, the service levels, and the inventory that
the present arrangement carries against what a well-run operation of comparable
size would expect to see. From that baseline we will identify the places where the
greatest improvement is available and describe, for each, what pursuing it would
ask of the organization and what it could reasonably be expected to return. We will
set the trade-offs out plainly, including those that a preferred course would ask you
to accept, rather than present a single answer as though it came without cost.
It is worth being equally plain about what this review is not. It is a diagnostic of the
supply chain and a set of recommendations grounded in it, and not a program to put
those recommendations into effect, nor a negotiation with your suppliers conducted
on your behalf; should you wish us to carry any recommendation through to

implementation, we would scope and price that as a separate engagement once the
review is complete. Should the scope of the work change materially once we are
underway, whether at your request or by what the analysis brings to light, we will
describe the change and settle its terms with you before we act on it, so that
nothing is added to the work without your assent.
The Team
You will work with a small and settled team, and the people whose names stand on
our analysis will be the people who have done it. Michael Walker, an engagement
manager of the firm, will run the work day to day and hold the relationship with
your people; he is the person to whom any question of scope, pace, or emphasis
should come, and the one who will answer for what we deliver. Deborah Gordon, an
associate, will lead the benchmarking and the cost and inventory analysis on which
the review rests, and will see that the figures we put before you can be defended
against a hard question. Daniel Leach, a research associate, will assemble the
underlying data and keep the trail by which each number can be traced back to the
source it came from.
Fees and Payment
Our fee for the review is fixed at $62,000, and it covers the work described above
together with the ordinary meetings, correspondence, and interim materials that
accompany it. It does not extend to work we may later agree to add, such as the
implementation of any recommendation, which we would scope and price separately
before beginning. We will invoice against the fixed fee at regular intervals as the
work proceeds, and each invoice falls due within thirty days of its date; because the
fee does not vary with the hours the work happens to take, you carry no exposure to
an overrun on our side.
Term and Termination
The engagement will commence on May 18, 2010 and is scoped to run for
approximately four months, that being the period over which we have planned the
diagnostic and the analysis, though I will tell you early if the work proves to need
more time or less. Either party may bring the engagement to an end on reasonable
written notice to the other. Should you elect to end it, you will owe our fee earned to
the date of termination together with any costs properly incurred to that point, and
nothing beyond; should we do so, which we would undertake only for a reason our
professional standards require, we will refund any part of the fixed fee that relates
to work not yet performed and will assist an orderly handover of the assignment.

Confidentiality
We will treat the information you place in our hands, together with the fact and the
substance of this engagement, as confidential, and we will use what you disclose to
us solely for the purpose of the review you have retained us to perform. We ask the
same of Poole, Mcknight and Rush with respect to the methods, analyses, and
materials we bring to the work. These obligations will survive the completion or
termination of the engagement, and neither party will disclose the other's
confidential information except where the law or a proper regulatory authority
compels it, and then only to the extent compelled and, where practicable, on notice
to the other.
Limitation of Liability
We will perform this engagement with the care and skill that our profession expects,
and our advice will represent our considered professional judgment on the
information available to us. We do not, however, warrant a particular commercial
result, since the benefit of a supply-chain review depends in large part on decisions
and actions that lie with your organization rather than with ours. Our aggregate
liability to you arising out of or in connection with this engagement will be limited to
the amount of the fee actually paid to us under it, save where the law does not
permit such a limit, and neither party will be liable to the other for indirect or
consequential loss.
Governing Law
This letter constitutes the entire agreement between us in respect of this
engagement and supersedes any prior discussion or understanding, and it may be
varied only by a writing signed by both parties. It will be governed by, and construed
in accordance with, the law of the state in which our firm maintains its principal
office, and each of us submits to the jurisdiction of the courts of that state in respect
of any dispute arising under it.
If the terms set out above reflect our agreement, I would ask you to countersign and
date the enclosed copy of this letter and return it to me, upon which we will confirm
the commencement and begin the work. If any part of it warrants discussion first,
tell me and I will make the time this week to talk it through before you sign.
Sincerely,
Julie Ramsey
Managing Principal
Calderwood Partners LLC
